A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original prediction correlations and molecular-simulation analyses on Protein G, Guerois and VAMP-seq.

after.justification: The original analyses remain, supplemented by ProteinMPNN, ESM2 and BioEmu evaluations and results on a subset of the mega-scale stability dataset.

M1.justification: V2 implements BioEmu-generated folded ensembles as an alternative to MD, whereas v1 only anticipated using generative ensemble models in its discussion. This adds a practical sampling route within the retained free-energy scoring framework; the principal scoring expressions and original unfolded-state estimators remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds a multi-protein subset of Tsuboyama et al.'s mega-scale stability dataset, accessed through ProteinGym and evaluated in Figure 2. This substantially broadens the represented proteins and high-throughput stability measurements beyond the retained Protein G, Guerois and VAMP-seq datasets.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds ProteinMPNN alongside ESM-IF on Protein G. Table 2 adds ESM2-based correction variants and sequence-only comparators using either amino-acid frequencies or ESM2, with several unfolded-state treatments. These expand the evaluated comparison methods; the newly discussed FoldX and Rosetta methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Added evaluations vary the inverse-folding model and ensemble generator on Protein G, and Figure 2 specifies 20 BioEmu samples for the new scaling experiment. Original filtering, correlation metrics and MD/MC settings remain. The NVT/NPT distinction in Appendix B.2 was already documented in v1, rather than introduced by this revision.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial tests of dependence on the inverse-folding model, replacement of MD by BioEmu, richer sequence corrections, and sequence-only versus structure-based scoring (Section 4.4, Tables 2–3 and Figure 6). The original per-protein breakdown and Pearson/Spearman comparison are retained or redisplayed, not new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 100 bootstrap samples for Figure 1 and report standard errors. V2 continues standard-error reporting in its added tables without stating a changed resampling procedure, repeated-run count, seed policy or significance-testing practice. Differences in individual reported standard errors concern results rather than statistical methodology.

E6.justification: Table 1 is numerically unchanged, but Tables 2–3 and Figure 2 add substantial results. On Protein G, ProteinMPNN scores 0.40 for single-structure scoring and 0.58 with MD plus IDP correction; ESM-IF scores 0.69 with BioEmu versus 0.70 with MD, reaching 0.72 with either ensemble plus IDP correction. Some repeated uncertainties conflict: the Protein G folded-only MD standard error is 0.03 in Table 1 but 0.02 in Tables 2–3.

T1.justification: Sections 2.3–3.1 replace the common-temperature assumption with potentially different latent temperatures and introduce explicit assumptions allowing temperature-conditioned likelihood ratios to be approximated by available models. Section 3.3.1 replaces the unfolded-structural-invariance justification with folding-probability regimes governing which pseudo-free-energy term dominates, illustrated in new Figure 3. The appendix monotonicity derivation is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and central thermodynamic-interpretation contribution remain. The introduction now explicitly claims gains using BioEmu, and the discussion changes computationally convenient folded-ensemble proxies from an anticipated possibility into a demonstrated result. This strengthens a practical contribution without redefining the paper's main objective.

C2.justification: Section 3.3.1 substantially narrows the justification for neglecting the unfolded term: it dominates for relatively stable variants, while folded-term dominance supports the approximation for strongly destabilizing mutations. V2 also interprets BioEmu as a scalable proxy and suggests structural information explains ESM2's disappointing corrections. However, its broad no-benefit wording overlooks VAMP-seq improvements from 0.51 to 0.59 for single-structure correction and 0.54 to 0.60 for ensemble correction.

D1.justification: V2 specifies 20 BioEmu samples for Figure 2 and discloses that autoregressive-order optimization was not implemented for the ProteinMPNN comparison. Conversely, it removes v1's exact ESM-IF checkpoint identifier and pretraining-source description. The existing simulation details, preprocessing instructions and Appendix C access information remain.

R1.justification: Section 5 expands from nearby inverse-folding studies to the history of statistical potentials and comparisons with FoldX and Rosetta, including their sensitivity to backbone templates. V2 also discusses Deng et al.'s subsequent fine-tuning work and adds references supporting the new models and benchmark. The Lewis reference is a publication update to an already cited work.

P1.justification: V2 polishes prose and terminology across the introduction, methods and discussion, consolidates author footnotes, and adds an Ablations and scaling subsection before Results. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain recognizable; much of the expansion documents scientific additions rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned with a structured formula matrix and Pearson-only plot; the original Pearson/Spearman comparison is redisplayed in Figure 5. The old per-protein Figure 2 becomes Figure 4. New Figures 2, 3 and 6 visualize scaling, theoretical regimes and ESM2 comparisons, while Tables 2–3 add structured comparisons and Table 1 is relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central argument by revising the temperature assumptions and replacing the broad unfolded-state-invariance justification with explicit applicability conditions. ProteinMPNN and BioEmu ablations, sequence-model controls and the additional multi-protein evaluation address important gaps in generality and practical feasibility left by v1. These gains outweigh localized weaknesses: overbroad ESM2 interpretation, inconsistent repeated standard errors, and loss of the exact ESM-IF checkpoint detail.
